Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 530 Moose Aerial Survey (2018) 
 
Background 
Wildlife Management Unit 530 (WMU 530) covers an area of 21,464 km2, with 7,074 km2 comprising caribou range 
and 732 km2 designated as a Key Wildlife and Biodiversity Zone. The WMU is delineated by the northwestern 
shoreline of Lake Athabasca, the interprovincial border with Saskatchewan to the east, the Clearwater River to the 
south, and the Athabasca River to the west. The boreal central mixedwood and the boreal Athabasca plain are the 
predominant subregions in the WMU, with a smaller portion of the boreal Peace-Athabasca delta and the 
Canadian Shield Kazan uplands subregions also represented. Lake Athabasca (2197 km2) and Richardson Lake 
(75 km2) are the largest waterbodies present. First Nations reserves present in WMU 530 include Athabasca 
Chipewyan First Nation, Fort McKay First Nation, and the Fort McMurray First Nation. 
A survey for moose was last conducted in the southern portion of WMU 530 (below latitude 57˚ 50” 0’) in 2010 
using the random stratified block methodology (Random Block). The moose population was estimated to have 
1211 individuals, a density of 0.11 moose/km2, and a bull:cow:calf ratio of 85:100:60 (Morgan and Powell 2010). 
See Table 1 for previous moose survey estimates for WMU 530 and surrounding WMUs. 
Hunting regulations for 2017 allowed for antlered moose to be harvested during an Archery Only Season (August 
25 – 31), and a split General Season with Special Licences (September 1- October 31 or November 1 – November 
30). 
The objective of the 2018 survey was to assess the status of the moose population in WMU 530 by determining 
estimates for abundance, density and the age-sex composition. 
 
Survey Method 
An aerial survey for moose was conducted from January 16th to 21st and from February 21st to 25th, 2018 in 
WMU 530. Based upon previous survey methods, the WMU was stratified between the northern and southern 
portions divided at 57˚ 50” 0’, where a change in habitat is noted; the south is dominated by the boreal central 
mixedwood natural subregion, while the north is dominated by the boreal Athabasca plain natural subregion. 493 
east-west transect lines (survey effort = 4,532 km) were flown using distance sampling techniques (Buckland et al., 
2001, 2010). Moose were classified by age class (adult or calf) and sex. Other wildlife sightings were recorded. 
 
WMU 530 North: The northern portion total area is 10,133 km2, however Lake Athabasca (2,197 km2) was 
removed from the total area, leaving 7,936 km2. 266 transects were flown for a total of 2,356 km of survey effort. 
Most transects were flown from February 21-25, 2018. 
 
WMU 530 South: The southern portion area is 11,330 km2. 227 transects were flown for a total of 2,177 km of 
survey effort. Most transects were flown from January 16-21, 2018.

Results 
A total of 342 moose were observed in 232 groups. The estimated density was 0.12 moose/km2 (90% CI 0.10 – 
0.14) and the estimated abundance was 2307 individuals (90% CI 1962 – 2713). The coefficient of variation for 
both density and abundance was 0.10 (Table 2). A total of 331 moose were successfully classified and the 
bull:cow:calf ratio was estimated to be 59:100:48. 
 
WMU 530 North: 124 moose were observed in 80 groups: 33 bulls (31 without antlers, 2 with antlers), 65 cows, 
and 26 calves. The estimated bull:cow:calf ratio was 51:100:40. The encounter rate was 0.03 moose/km2 (90% CI 
0.03 – 0.04). The estimated density was 0.07 moose/km2 (90% CI 0.06 – 0.09; CV = 0.15). The estimated 
abundance in the northern portion was 589 individuals (90% CI 463 – 750). See Table 2. 
 
WMU 530 South: 218 moose were observed in 152 groups: 61 bulls (43 without antlers, 18 with antlers), 95 cows, 
51 calves, and 11 unclassified. The estimated bull:cow:calf ratio was 64:100:54. The encounter rate was 0.07 
moose/km2 (90% CI 0.06 – 0.08). The estimated density was 0.15 moose/km2 (90% CI 0.12 – 0.18; CV = 0.11). 
The estimated abundance in the southern portion was 1718 individuals (90% CI 1426 – 2071). See Table 2.
